prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: how did the 2025 sales funnel convert? Take the leads created in 2025 (created_at, Brussels local time). A contact is one email address, compared exactly as stored. A contact counts as with_opportunity when one of those leads has an opportunity, and as won when one of those opportunities is won. The steps need no date order: an opportunity counts whenever it was created, and a won one whenever it closed, even in a later year. Return four columns, in this order: contacts, with_opportunity, won (each a number of contacts) and win_rate, won over with_opportunity, as a fraction between 0 and 1. Return one row. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check what the win rate is divided by: the question names the step before it.
The win rate is a step rate: the won contacts over the contacts with an opportunity, not over every contact.
starter_sql:
WITH lead_steps AS (  -- one row per lead created in the period, with its opportunity if any
  SELECT l.email, o.opportunity_id, o.is_won
  FROM leads l
  LEFT JOIN opportunities o ON o.lead_id = l.lead_id
  WHERE l.created_at >= TIMESTAMP '2025-01-01 00:00:00' AND l.created_at < TIMESTAMP '2026-01-01 00:00:00'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS contacts,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN opportunity_id IS NOT NULL THEN email END) AS with_opportunity,
       COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_won THEN email END) AS won,
       1.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN is_won THEN email END) / COUNT(DISTINCT email) AS win_rate
FROM lead_steps
why_this_works: A step rate divides by the step right before it, so the win rate uses the contacts with an opportunity as its base.
